full_judgment:
The prosecution case was that a holding recorded in Khatian No. 447/10 of Village Jalalabad belonged to the complainant P. W. 1 Aqsad Ali. The rent for the years 1363-66 B. S. of that holding fell in arrear. Certificate Case No. 49119/60-61 was thereupon started and notice thereof was duly served on Aqsad Ali. On 16.6.61 Aqsed Ali remitted the certificate dues amounting to Rs. 18.96 as mentioned in the said notice. This remittance duly reached the office of the Sub-Divisional Manager, who was also the Certificate Officer. lnspite of the receipt of the money, the holding was sold at auction and purchased by the Government. Delivery of possession was taken on behalf of Government by the Tahsildar, that is, the appellant on 17. 11. 62. Thereafter Aqsed Ali submitted a petition on 26. 11. 62 to the Sub-Divisional Manager complaining that inspite of payment of dues, his holding was sold at auction. On that very date (26.11.62) the Nazir of the Sub-Divisional Manager on verification submitted a note to the Sub-Divisional Manager to the effect that the certificate dues were duly received by a money order on 20. 6. 61. The said rote also contained recommendation that the certificate case be shown as satisfied and the certificate costs be realised from the dealing assistant. Aqsed Ali could not, however, know what had happened to his petition addressed to the Sub-Divisional Manager. About one year after, the appellant Tahsildar sent for Aqsed Ali and suggested that he should take fresh settlement of the holding which was auction-purchased in a certificate sale and delivery of possession was taken by Government. He first demanded Rs. 130/- but the amount was settled at Rs. 100/-. Aqsed Ali took time and having borrowed that amount from his relation P. W. 5 Abdur Rahman Gazi met the appellant in the Talisil Office on 4.11. 63. The amount of Rs. 100/- was paid to the appellant who did not grant any receipt to Aqsed Ali on that day. He asked Aqsed Ali to take the receipt 3 or 4 days after. He went to the Tahsil Office as directed. The appellant gave him a dakhila. Aqsed Ali being illiterate showed the dakhila to his neighbour who told him that it was a receipt for Rs. 18.07 only. Thereupon he met the appellant again and asked him as to why receipt was granted for Rs.18.08 and not for Rs. 100/- realised from him. The appellant told him that .06 acre more of his land was made khas by the Government and that he would get settlement of that land as well but the appellant Tahsildar neither gave him the said land nor returned the money. Later Aqsed Ali sent another petition to the Sub-Divisional Manager by registered post on 24. 2.64 informing him of the matter but having received no reply from the office of the Sub-Divisional Manager, he submitted a petition on 7. 4. 65 to the Anti-Corruption Officer at Khulna whereupon an inquiry was held by an Assistant Inspector D. A. B., Sathkhira, who seized the dakhila from Aqsed Ali on 13. 5. 65 and also the records of the certificate case and the other papers from the office of the Sub-Divisional Manager and thereupon a regular case was started at Molaroa Police Station. Having completed the investigation the charge-sheet was submitted upon obtaining sanction from the proper authority. 

 The defence case was that Aqsed Ali paid the appellant a lump sum of, Rs. 100/- in a G. C. Note towards the rental of the aforesaid holding as well as for settlement of .06 acre of land more. The appellant had DO authority to settle khas land with the complainant. He did not return the balance money out of the said amount of Rs. 100/- after realising the rental of the holding amount to Rs. 18.07 and told him that he would give him receipt and the balance money later on as he had no change with him at that time. Subsequently the appellant had altercation with Aqsed Ali over the matter of the settlement of the aforesaid land measuring .06 acre. The appellant, due to altercation, turned Aqsed Ali out of the Tahsil Office when he was threatened by Aqsed Ali that he would teach him a good lesson. The appellant had thus been falsely implicated out of grudge. 

 Now we propose to re-examine the evidence adduced by the prosecution with a view to see whether the prosecution has established the charge of cheating against the appellant. The prosecution case was that the appellant Tahsildar called Aqsed Ali to his office in November. 1963 and told him that his holding having been made khas, he could get fresh settlement if he so liked. For that purpose it was settled. that a sum of Rs.100/- would be paid. The said amount was actually paid to the appellant who later granted Aqsed Ali a dakhila for Rs. 18.07 which was the rental dues of the holding. For the balance amounting to Rs.81.93 the appellant did not grant any receipt nor he returned the said amount. The prosecution alleged that the appellant deceitfully realised that amount from Aqsed Ali. P.W.1 Aqsed Ali deposed to that effect P.W.2 Raushan Ali deposed that Aqsed Ali gave the appellant Rs.100/- in his presence in Jalalabad Tahsil Office. The payment was made to settle the matter of Aqsed's land which had been allegedly made khas. At that time P.W.3 Manik and P.W.6 Badruddin were also present and witnessed the payment. The Tahsildar did not give any receipt or dakhila but asked him to take the dakhila 3 days after, P.W.3 Manik deposed that the appellant told that Rs. 130/- would be required but ultimately Aqsed Ali paid the appellant a hundred rupee G. C. Note. The appellant did not give any receipt but asked Aqsed Ali to get the receipt 3/4 days after P W. 6 Badruddiu deposed that Aqsed Ali settled the matter with the appellant to make his land free from liability paying Rs.100/- in his presence in the Tahsil Office P.W's Baushan and N. Manik also witnessed the payment. The appellant did not give any receipt and said that it would be given on getting a receipt book. He also deposed that rent due was Rs. 18/- and a Jump of Rs. 100/- was paid as there had been an auction sale of the holding and everything was to be cleared up. It was contended on behalf of the appellant that though P.W.2 Raushan and P.W.6 Baduruddin deposed as eye-witnesses to the occurrence, they were not, in fact, eye-witnesses, Mr. Rab referred to the cross-examination of P.W.1 who appears to have said that he did not see Raushan and Badaruddin in the office while he paid the money to the appellant. Now the question is whether Baushan and Badaruddin should be disbelieved and their evidence discarded in view of the statement of P.W.1 in his cross-examination that he did not see Raushan and Badaruddin when he made the payment. In his examination-in-chief, however P.W.1 said that many persons were present when be paid the amount or Rs.100/- P.W.1 might have missed noticing P.Ws. Raushan and Badruddin among many others who were in the office. We are of the view that there is 110 reason to disbelieve P.Ws. Raushan and Badaruddin, and discard their evidence as regards payment of Rs.100/-. It may be noted that there is nothing on record to indicate that P.Ws. Raushan and Badaruddin were in any manner interested in the prosecution and falsely supported. As regards P.W.3 Manik, Mr. Rab submitted that he supported the defence case as he said in cross-examination that the appellant demanded Rs.18.07 and not an amount of Rs,100/-. P.
